items.problem: The migrated UI preserved structure but changed the source's dark theme and lightweight heading treatment to light/bold defaults.
items.evidence: migration-score.json: both features partial; discrepancies.json: two major visual discrepancies. Source SharedContent/xaml/App.xaml line 18 has RequestedTheme="Dark" while migrated App.xaml has no RequestedTheme; migrated styles still inherit WinUI TitleTextBlockStyle.
items.covered_at: SKILL.md#Principles and #Critical-Rules / Fidelity; MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md#xaml and Resource references
items.proposed_improvement: Make visual semantics an explicit fidelity invariant: preserve RequestedTheme, explicit colors/weights/sizes, and verify inherited platform styles because same-named UWP and WinUI theme resources can resolve to different effective typography or brushes.
items.generalizes: Theme roots and platform style aliases occur in most XAML apps; namespace-correct markup can still produce a broad visual redesign.

items.problem: The CaptureElement replacement renamed the element but left stale PreviewControl references in code-behind.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 4208-4209 and 4238-4265: CS0103 remained for two PreviewControl references after applying #capture.
items.covered_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md#capture, especially the XAML swap at lines 62-68
items.proposed_improvement: Remove the contradictory instruction to preserve the XAML name while the sample renames it, and require a scoped search that updates every code-behind reference after an element-level swap.
items.generalizes: Any XAML control replacement with a changed name or type can leave compile-time or runtime references in event handlers, transforms, bindings, and visual-state targets.
